plan.summary: From Dots' audit of the four Oct 21 ChatGPT reports and two Gemini reports, each quote re-read at its page (Forbes items rest on Dots' read of the publisher's text; Forbes blocks this machine). Old values from the private core data at ede3b1d. Dorian Gray's amended Form D: $8,297,262 raised of an $8.75M maximum, with Broadway News as the recoupment source. SpongeBob $800K weekly operating costs (Forbes). New: The Inheritance (up to $9.85M, did not recoup per Forbes, author a co-producer) and West Side Story 2020 (up to $16M, budget only).
steps: Dorian Gray SEC amount, SpongeBob weekly cost
Add The Inheritance and West Side Story 2020

actions.description: the-picture-of-dorian-gray-2025: the amount the amended filing says was raised

actions.newValue: SEC Form D/A (Dorian Broadway Limited Partnership, CIK 0002035619, signed Apr 21, 2025): total offering $8,750,000, total sold $8,297,262; "Maximum capitalization was $8,750,000/Minimum capitalization was $7,750,000/Offering capitalized at $8,297,262". Broadway News reported the $8.75 million maximum as its capitalization. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2035619/000203561925000001/primary_doc.xml

actions.oldValue: Playbill article stating the show recouped its investment in its final week on Broadway
actions.newValue: Broadway News (Jul 2, 2025): "The Broadway mounting of 'The Picture of Dorian Gray' has recouped its investment." It recouped in its final week (ended Jun 29, 2025). https://www.broadwaynews.com/the-picture-of-dorian-gray-recoups-broadway-investment/

actions.description: the-picture-of-dorian-gray-2025: SEC and trade sources replace the Reddit threads

actions.newValue: Forbes (Lee Seymour, Sep 20, 2018, 'Three Broadway musicals closed last week'): weekly operating costs of $800,000 for SpongeBob SquarePants. https://www.forbes.com/sites/leeseymour/2018/09/20/three-broadway-musicals-closed-last-week-what-happened/

actions.description: spongebob-squarepants-2017: operating costs, not an all-in break-even

entry.recoupedSource: Forbes (Lee Seymour, Jun 29, 2021): The Inheritance did not recoup its Broadway capital. The author discloses he was one of its producers. https://www.forbes.com/sites/leeseymour/2021/06/29/harry-potter-returns-to-broadway-with-a-facelift/
entry.capitalizationSource: Broadway News (Feb 20, 2020): "The play was capitalized for up to $9.85 million, according to a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission." TheaterMania (Mar 13, 2020) put it at around $9 million; Broadway Journal reported a $10 million budget. https://www.broadwaynews.com/the-inheritance-will-end-its-broadway-run-in-march/
entry.notes: Matthew Lopez's two-part play at the Ethel Barrymore (opened Nov 17, 2019), Tony winner for Best Play. It had already set a Mar 15, 2020 closing when the shutdown ended the run on Mar 11. Capitalized for up to $9.85 million; it did not recoup.

entry.capitalizationSource: Broadway News (Jul 13, 2021): "The show was capitalized for up to $16 million." CBS's 60 Minutes (Feb 16, 2020) said the production cost more than $15 million. https://www.broadwaynews.com/west-side-story-hangmen-receive-government-boost-for-reopening/
entry.notes: Ivo van Hove's revival at the Broadway Theatre (opened Feb 20, 2020), stopped by the Mar 2020 shutdown after 24 regular performances and never reopened. Capitalized for up to $16 million; it received a $10 million Shuttered Venue Operators Grant. No investor outcome has been reported.
